blocks.text: What Is Paint Finish?

Paint finish, or a paint’s sheen, is basically the amount of light reflection from a painted surface. It identifies paints that reflect light and those that absorb it. Finishes are broadly classified into two categories: matte or flat paints (which absorb more light than they reflect), and semi-gloss or gloss paints (which reflect light, resulting in a shiny finish).

blocks.text: Make Sure the Paint Finish Can Withstand the Elements

Climate and weather are two of the biggest factors to consider when choosing a paint finish for your outdoor spaces. For example, if you live in an area with a lot of rain, you’ll want to select a paint finish with excellent water resistance that can prevent mold and mildew growth, such as a hi-gloss. Choosing a flat or matte finish in such a climate would not be ideal as it can absorb moisture and lead to early damage and frequent touch-ups.

blocks.text: Ensure It Can Endure Your Cleaning Routine

Water and cleaning agents can strip off the paint finish on your outdoor spaces, especially if you use harsh chemicals or scrub too vigorously. Choosing a paint finish that can withstand your cleaning routine is crucial. If your outdoor space encounters heavy foot traffic daily and needs frequent cleaning, consider a durable and washable finish, such as a semi-gloss or hi-gloss.

blocks.text: Now that you understand the critical factors you must consider when choosing a paint finish for your outdoor spaces let’s explore the common types of finishes available:

blocks.text: Flat or Matte: This finish offers a smooth and non-reflective surface. It’s perfect for hiding imperfections on walls or fences, but it’s not very durable and can quickly fade or stain. A matte finish is ideal for old structures to hide their age and flaws.
blocks.html: Flat or Matte: This finish offers a smooth and non-reflective surface. It’s perfect for hiding imperfections on walls or fences, but it’s not very durable and can quickly fade or stain. A matte finish is ideal for old structures to hide their age and flaws.

blocks.text: Low-Luster: This finish is a step above matte. It provides sufficient shine and is more durable, making it suitable for outdoor furniture or trim. However, it can also wash away quickly with frequent washing.

blocks.text: Satin: A satin finish is the middle point between matte and glossy. It offers a subtle shine and is somewhat durable, making it an excellent choice for high-traffic areas like decks or patios.

blocks.text: Glossy: Glossy finishes are subdivided into two categories: semi-gloss and hi-gloss. Both offer a high shine and are highly durable, making them ideal for outdoor structures and furniture. However, glossy finishes can’t conceal imperfections and require proper surface preparation.
